newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair eyes legal action on Schiphol night ban.
newsitem.headline: Martinair eyes legal action on Schiphol night ban.

text.p: Dutch airline Martinair NV is considering taking legal action against Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport following the airport's announcement on Friday of a night ban on some freighter operations from August 1, an airline spokesman said.

Earlier on Friday Aero Groundservices BV, the leading Dutch cargo handling company, said it is also considering legal action. KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, which owns 50 percent of Martinair, said the proposed move is unacceptable on both commercial and operational grounds.
A Martinair spokesman said the takeoff ban hits both the cargo and passenger operations of Martinair.

Under the summer schedule at least two Boeing 727-200 freighter frequencies are effected and in winter this is likely to be four a week, he said. He said it is not just the flights that cannot takeoff in the night that are hit, but the whole of the airline's schedule. "It has a snowball effect."

"Our B747-200s are also certified (Chapter 3), quieter, aircraft by the Dutch civil aviation authority and the aircraft manufacturer, Boeing. My argument is that they cannot ban operations by these quieter aircraft," he said.
He said that the carrier had had no warning of the ban and is considering many options, including legal action.

Airlines operating from Schiphol have been stunned by today's announcement that from August 1, aircraft such as the McDonnell Douglas Corp's DC-10 and Boeing Co's 747 in its 100,200, 300 and SP versions will not be allowed to take off from the main Dutch airport between 2300 hours and 0600 hours local time.
The reminaing 50 percent shareholding in Martinair is held by Nedlloyd.
